what: O4 §九 gate codings for the items the §五 instrument contract did not already cover. Sealed BEFORE any gate pixel is captured, in its own commit, for the same reason §五 was sealed before the factorial: a coding written after seeing a candidate is not a coding, it is a result.
whyASeparateCommit: §十三's five commits are described as suggested. Writing these codings into the evidence commit would place them, in the record, after the pixels they judge. One extra clearly-named pre-registration commit is the cheaper honesty.

primaryGate.state: System B OFF (envMixScale 0, rimScale 0, shell off), labels off, deterministic frozen media, reflectionSupport=geometry, dispersionLaw=o1-spectral

item1.rule: body floor reduced by >= 40% of the accepted local floor

item2.rule: abs(candidate - target) <= max(2 x Target repeatability, 1.5 px)
item2.repeatabilitySource: qa-v5/optics-o3/target-repeatability.json -- byte-identical repeats, spread 0, so the floor binds
item2.note: this is a two-sided window. Undershooting the Target is as much a miss as overshooting it, and is scored as one.

item3.rule: dark-side body luma moves TOWARD the Target's dark-side edge luma
item3.targetLumaBasisNote: 48.1 is the Target's full render; the Target has no System-B-off mode to capture, so this item is scored as DIRECTION only, exactly as §九.3 words it.

mobile.rule: same direction, and enter the same 1.5 px window against that viewport's own Target anchor

item4.title: grayscale does not add colour
item4.coding: edgeChromaMean and interiorChromaMean, candidate vs control. The media is achromatic through the media-only path, so any chroma here is shader-introduced.
item4.thresholdOrigin: the O2-recorded deterministic <=1/255-per-channel shader-program envelope, expressed on a 0-255 chroma mean; reused unchanged from O3 items 8/9.

item5.title: no increase in broad coloured rim
item5.coding: fringeRB and fringeWidthPxMean, candidate vs control
item5.pass: candidate <= control + 0.5 on BOTH, on every asset

item6.title: HF checker preserves or improves local high-frequency structure
item6.coding: hfEnergy = mean absolute 4-neighbour Laplacian of luma over the card interior (middle 55%). Higher means more surviving high-frequency structure. Reported for the media-only frame too, which is the unblurred ideal.
item6.why: 'preserve or improve' is a one-sided test: the candidate may sharpen, and must not smear. The 2% allowance is the same order as the shader-program envelope above.

item7.title: interior media within sealed tolerance
item7.coding: o4_instruments.interior_change(control, candidate) on every scored desktop asset -- the baseline-aware branch sealed in the instrument contract

item8.title: media-only exact zero
item8.pass: differingPixels == 0 exactly; the body change is not in the media path at all

item9.title: true gutter unchanged
item9.coding: o4_instruments.gutter_pair_outside_silhouette against the TRUE silhouette derived from the control lane
item9.why: a body-colour change cannot legitimately alter a pixel the glass does not cover, so the correct threshold is zero, not a tolerance.

item10.title: no temporal pop
item10.coding: the O3 pop coding, unchanged: per recorded frame, the full-frame count of bright low-chroma pixels (luma > 200, chroma < 40); no adjacent-frame relative change above 40%, and no frame at zero between two non-zero neighbours

item11.title: control lane exact zero vs the accepted baseline
item11.coding: bodyFloorMode=current vs a worktree build of e913aa6a33e384ba4fc80eb28b9a8718fb20e5b9, System B OFF, labels off, same frozen media, every scored viewport

prohibited: changing any threshold above after gate pixels exist
substituting a different measurand for a failing one
